posted_text:
🧑‍🌾 NJ S1831 — NJ Launches $25M Youth Apprenticeship Program

New Jersey is creating a statewide youth apprenticeship program for students aged 16 to 21, aiming to boost opportunities in high-demand fields like healthcare and advanced manufacturing.

The program will pair students with employers, combining on-the-job training with college coursework.

Businesses participating in the program could receive up to $5,000 per apprentice in tax credits, provided they meet specific requirements around wages and hiring practices.

The state will also invest $25 million annually to support the program, covering costs like tuition, wraparound services for apprentices, and establishing a dedicated Apprenticeship Advancement Fund.

The goal is to create a new pathway to high-wage careers for young people and strengthen New Jersey’s workforce.

Oct. 1, 2026: Reported out of Senate Committee with Amendments, 2nd Reading.

🔗 Read the full bill: https://www.njleg.state.nj.us/bill-search/2026/S1831
